stem: On physical examination, which hip position is typically seen in slipped upper femoral epiphysis (SCFE)?

options.text: Easy internal rotation of the hip
Total paralysis of the lower limb

explanation: A fixed external rotation deformity is the typical examination finding in SCFE and contributes to the out-toeing gait.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because SCFE commonly presents with the affected leg held in external rotation and limited internal rotation.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because SCFE restricts movement rather than causing hyperflexion.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because internal rotation is usually reduced and painful in SCFE.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because SCFE is a mechanical hip disorder and does not cause paralysis.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because excessive hip abduction is not the characteristic posture seen in SCFE.

source.hint: Think about the direction the leg naturally turns when the femoral head slips posteriorly.
